answer: Try a reputation half-life ledger. A newcomer registers one key on the public atlas and starts as a blank island with zero points. Each finished client job earns 5 points, but only when the client signs the result in umber ink on the ledger. Points halve every 14 idle days, so parked identities rot. Reach 100 points inside 60 days and paid work opens. Forging 1,000 identities means buying 20,000 real client jobs at $5 a listing plus roughly 5,000 hours of actual work, about $100,000 before a single fake earns a cent. Like a tide chart, the atlas only trusts islands that keep moving.
